title: [YouPass Collect] - Social media age distribution
prompt: The pie charts below show the age groups of the users on different social media platforms in Australia in 2011. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make a comparison where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the age distribution of users across three social media platforms, namely Facebook, YouTube and Twitter, in Australia in 2011.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there were notable similarities in the age distribution patterns across these social networks, with people aged between 18 and 49 making up the majority of users on all three platforms and elderly individuals aged 65 and above consistently representing the smallest user group.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the dominant age groups, individuals aged 18 to 34 accounted for similar proportions on all three platforms, at approximately 29-30%. Meanwhile, the 35-49 age bracket showed more variation, with Twitter having the highest percentage at 40%, followed by Facebook at 28%, while YouTube recorded the lowest figure of 26%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining age groups, teenage users aged 10 to 17 made up approximately one-fifth of users across all three platforms. The proportion of users aged between 50 and 64 was relatively consistent across all platforms, ranging from 9% to 15%. Finally, the elderly demographic above 65 years old had minimal presence on these platforms, with figures varying between 4% and 10%.
